name: Duxbury
seo_title: Christmas Events for Kids in Duxbury, MA 2026
seo_desc: Kids' Christmas in Duxbury, MA: Holly Days trolleys, the Festival of Lights, Alden House, a Nutcracker and historic house family days.
lede: Duxbury celebrates Christmas village by village, with a Holly Days trolley afternoon, a Rotary tree and menorah lighting on the Town Green, historic house tours and a Nutcracker on Alden Street.
celebrates: Holly Days is the town's signature day, with trolleys linking Duxbury's villages and family activities, performances and holiday cheer at every stop. The Duxbury Chamber of Commerce says the event has been funded entirely by sponsorships and donations since 2014. The Rotary Club of Duxbury adds a Festival of Lights with a tree and menorah lighting on the Town Green, the Duxbury High School Chorus and Santa. Historic sites join in too, with candle dipping at the Alden House, decorated rooms at the King Caesar House and holiday family programs at the Art Complex Museum.
lastyear: The Duxbury Chamber of Commerce says the Holly Days trolleys carry more than 1,000 people through town during the event. In 2025 the Rotary Club's Festival of Lights went ahead in the rain, with games, face painting, food, music and the Duxbury High School Chorus. Santa and Mrs. Claus lit the Christmas trees and the menorah with the help of three young Duxbury citizens, and a bubble machine left a carpet of bubbles on the ground for kids.
facts: The Alden House Historic Site stands on part of the original land grant given to John and Priscilla Alden in 1627. It became a National Historic Landmark in 2008, and the Alden Kindred of America opens it for holiday programs. The Rotary Club of Duxbury celebrated the 74th anniversary of its original charter in June 2025, and its Festival of Lights photo albums on its website go back to 2023.
trains: Duxbury does not have an MBTA Commuter Rail station of its own. The MBTA's Kingston Line serves the South Shore to the south of town, and the line page lists the stops and schedules. For a train ride at Christmas, Edaville in Carver runs holiday trains through Christmas lights, and the Boston Street Railway Association keeps historic streetcars in the Boston area.

faq: Holly Days is a community holiday event in which trolleys carry families to stops in all of Duxbury's villages. The official site promises family friendly activities, live performances and holiday cheer at every stop, from local crafts and seasonal treats to music and community gatherings. It is funded through sponsorships and donations and run by the Duxbury Chamber of Commerce.
Does Duxbury have a Christmas tree lighting?

Yes. The Rotary Club of Duxbury hosts a Festival of Lights on the Town Green, with a Christmas tree and menorah lighting. Its flyer lists the Duxbury High School Chorus and Santa Claus, plus a free cookie and cup of cocoa while supplies last. Check the club's website each year for the date and time.
Where can kids see Santa in Duxbury?

Santa appears at the Rotary Club's Festival of Lights on the Town Green according to the club's flyer. Its recap of the 2025 festival also describes Santa and Mrs. Claus listening to children and lighting the trees. The Plymouth Area Chamber's Holly Days post also mentions a photo with Santa inside the Depot building, so check the chamber site.
Is there a Nutcracker in Duxbury?

Yes. SSC School of Dance, part of the South Shore Conservatory, presents The Nutcracker at the Duxbury Performing Arts Center on Alden Street. The conservatory describes it as a story that begins on Christmas Eve, with dancing snowflakes, toy soldiers and the Land of Sweets. Tickets are sold through its online box office.
Can I take a train to Duxbury at Christmas?

Duxbury has no Commuter Rail station, so most families drive. The MBTA's Kingston Line serves nearby South Shore towns. For a holiday train ride, look at Edaville in Carver, and see our museum pages for other train attractions around Boston.
